Subject: URGENT: Sudden 5xx spike + request throttling — Portage production (US-WEST-2 / AZ2)

Mateo —

We started seeing a large increase in 5xx responses and token throttling from your API in AZ2 starting ~07:40 PDT. Error rate peaked at ~18% and tail latency is up to 5s for some interactive sessions. Our checkout flows are timing out and we're getting dozens of customer complaints. We tried failing over to our secondary region but the behavior appears to persist for requests proxied through Redwood AZ2.

Can we get an immediate status and an ETA for remediation? We're on-call and can jump on a call. This is impacting revenue and senior execs are monitoring.

Attachments: portage_alert_screens_0502.png (referenced)

— Ellen

On Tue, May 2, 2028 at 08:32 AM mateo_alvarez@redwood.ai wrote:
> Folks — forwarding Portage's alert. High severity customer, enterprise contract (DEAL-6732).

They reported the spike at ~07:40 PDT. We already pulled early metrics: AZ2's NAT gateway (egress) is saturating for ERR (external vendor) connections; we see connection resets and a sudden drop in keepalive utilization which correlates to 502/504 and internal 5xx. Concurrently, a backend KV node in AZ2 entered GC pauses (long-tail) and amplified latency for batched requests.

Immediate mitigations we recommend (and are ready to start):
1) Enable region-wide traffic steering: route new Portage sessions to US-WEST-1 and US-EAST-1 for the next 90 minutes. (We have route policy ready: portage-steer-0502).
2) Apply egress backpressure: reduce concurrent outbound pipeline to the offending vendor to avoid connection resets.
3) Grey release patch to KV node to force GC-friendly compaction (low risk, 60s window).
4) Enable aggressive prefix/KV caching for Portage to reduce token regen calls (fast toggle).

We need explicit approval from account + exec (for cross-region steer). If approved, ops can start routing changes within 5 minutes and we will monitor the error rate drop. I'll spin up a bridge and start the runbook (playbook_az2_egress_patch.pdf attached).

Sergio
Senior SRE, Redwood Inference

Subject: Incident update — Redwood API disruption in US-WEST-2 (AZ2)

Ellen / Jamil —

Thanks for the quick flag. We believe the issue is an egress saturation in AZ2 that is causing connection resets to your downstream vendors and amplifying an already-hot KV node in the same AZ. Our SREs are executing the following now:

1) Active traffic steering: new Portage sessions are being routed to US-WEST-1 and US-EAST-1. Steering is live as of 09:20 PDT.
2) Caching and rate limits: we have toggled aggressive prefix/KV caching for your account and temporarily reduced concurrent outbound pipeline to the problematic vendor.
3) Node remediation: we are performing a low-risk compaction on the impacted backend node; this should finish within 5–10 minutes.

We will monitor error rates and latency and update you at +15m. Link to live incident page: https://status.redwood.ai/incidents/PORTAGE-az2-egress-0502. Bridge is open if you'd like to join (zoom.us/j/xxxxxx).

We take this seriously and will provide a formal post-mortem once stabilized. Aditya has proposed a remediation credit; we will follow up with specifics once we have a stability window.

Apologies for the disruption — we are on it.

— Mateo Alvarez
Account Lead, Redwood Inference
